title: Complementary differential basis after a further principal shrink
statement: theorem exists_smooth_split_complement_shrink (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v) [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] (a : A) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (ha : a ∉ p) (n c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ n) (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (Localization.Away a) M] (b : Module.Basis (Fin c) (Localization.Away a) M) (hsm : Smooth R (Localization.Away a)) (hsplit : Nonempty ((M × KaehlerDifferential R (Localization.Away a)) ≃ₗ[Localization.Away a] (Fin n → Localization.Away a))) : ∃ t : A, t ∉ p ∧ Smooth R (Localization.Away (a * t)) ∧ Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin (n - c)) (Localization.Away (a * t)) (KaehlerDifferential R (Localization.Away (a * t))))

source.place: Tag 07C6, proof, especially the replacement of a by a times a further element outside the prime

proof.text: Extend the prime to A[1/a], using disjointness of its powers from the prime. The smooth differential module is finite projective, and its localization at this prime is free by Mathlib Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing.

Base change the given split equivalence and the conormal basis to the local ring. TensorProduct.prodRight and finrank_prod give c + rank(differentials) = n, hence the rank is n-c. Reindex the finite local basis.

Use Module.FinitePresentation.exists_basis_localizedModule_powers to spread that rank-n-c basis to a principal open of A[1/a]. Take the numerator t of the localization element; associated elements belong to the same ideals, so t is outside the original prime.

Use IsLocalization.Away.mul_of_associated to identify the iterated localization with A[1/(a*t)]. Transport the basis by tensor base change and KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale. Smoothness follows by composition with principal localization.
